key_insight: Differentiable foundation models enable joint optimization of crystal composition and structure to design semiconductors with band gaps targeted for photovoltaic absorption.
engineering_relevance: The approach could accelerate solar-absorber screening by optimizing electronic properties alongside an energy-based stability penalty.
method: Extend pretrained EquiformerV3 to continuous species weights and site occupancies without retraining on fractional data.
Use property-model gradients and an energy penalty to jointly update composition, atom count, positions, and lattice vectors.
Validate candidate band gaps and stability with SCAN calculations and assess finite-temperature competition.
evidence_signal: SCAN calculations confirmed ten novel semiconductor structures with gaps within 20% of a 1.34 eV target on their respective raw or empirically corrected scales, all within 70 meV/atom of the DFT hull.
watch_item: Training-functional band-gap bias propagates into designs unless corrected in the objective; target gaps alone do not establish solar-cell performance.
paper_title: Inverse design of superconductors and semiconductors with differentiable foundation models
